title: API Gateways, Service Mesh & Edge
summary: One front door for the outside world, and an invisible nervous system between your services — learn which job belongs to which.

blocks.markdown:
Two different proxies do the boring shared work so your services stay focused on business logic.

- An **API gateway** is the single front door for traffic coming *in* from clients — it sits at the edge.
- A **service mesh** handles traffic *between* your own services, via a small proxy beside each one.
- **North-south** = in/out of the system (client ↔ gateway). **East-west** = service ↔ service inside (mesh).
- They're **complementary**, not competitors. Big systems run both.

blocks.subTitle: Which one do I reach for?
blocks.markdown:
Match the job to the tool.

| Need | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Auth, rate-limit, TLS for clients | API gateway |
| One frontend wants a custom API | BFF |
| mTLS + retries between services | Service mesh |
| Just 3 services | Plain LB, skip mesh |
| Edge security + internal zero-trust | Gateway + mesh |

blocks.subTitle: The API gateway
blocks.markdown:
The gateway is a reverse proxy at the edge that does cross-cutting work once, before any service sees the request.

![API gateway fronting services, north-south traffic](assets/e05-api-gateways-service-mesh/api-gateway.svg)

- **TLS termination** — decrypts HTTPS in one tuned place, so services don't each manage certs.
- **Auth** — validates a JWT or API key; a bad token gets a 401 before any service is touched.
- **Rate limiting** — counts requests per key, rejects excess with 429 (token bucket or sliding window).
- **Routing** — matches path/host (`/orders/*` → Orders) and forwards.

assets.alt: API gateway fronting services, north-south traffic

blocks.subTitle: Request aggregation & the BFF
blocks.markdown:
A plain gateway gives every client the *same* API; a BFF shapes it per client.

- **Aggregation** — for one client call, the gateway fans out to several services and combines responses, so a mobile app makes 1 request instead of 5.
- **BFF (Backend-for-Frontend)** — a dedicated gateway *per client type*. The mobile BFF trims fields and round trips; the web BFF does its own thing.
- Each frontend team owns its BFF, so no shared bottleneck — at the cost of more services to run.

blocks.subTitle: The service mesh
blocks.markdown:
The mesh injects a sidecar proxy (usually **Envoy**) next to every service; all internal calls go proxy-to-proxy.

![Service mesh with sidecar proxies and control plane](assets/e05-api-gateways-service-mesh/service-mesh.svg)

- The app dials normally, but **iptables** silently redirects the call into the local sidecar.
- The sidecar opens **mTLS** to the destination's sidecar — encrypted, both ends identified.
- It applies **retries**, **timeouts**, **circuit breaking**, **load balancing**, and **traffic shifting**.
- It emits **metrics, logs, and traces** for every call — uniform observability, zero app code.

assets.alt: Service mesh with sidecar proxies and control plane

blocks.subTitle: Data plane vs control plane
blocks.markdown:
The mesh splits into two layers — and the brain stays out of the request path.

- **Data plane** — the fleet of sidecars that actually carries the traffic.
- **Control plane** — the brain (e.g. Istio's `istiod`). You write one rule, it compiles it to Envoy config and pushes it to every sidecar, along with rotating certs.
- It is **not** in the request path. If it dies, existing sidecars keep serving on last-known config — you only lose the ability to *change* config or onboard new pods.

blocks.subTitle: Gateway + mesh together
blocks.markdown:
In a large system both exist: the gateway is the secure edge, the mesh runs everything inside.

![API gateway at the edge feeding into a service mesh](assets/e05-api-gateways-service-mesh/gateway-plus-mesh.svg)

- A client enters through the gateway (**north-south**), then the request travels service-to-service over mTLS inside the mesh (**east-west**).
- One handles "outside-in," the other "inside-inside."
- Modern setups use an Envoy-based **mesh ingress gateway** that is both — edge entry *and* a mesh participant.

assets.alt: API gateway at the edge feeding into a service mesh

blocks.subTitle: What you trade
blocks.markdown:
Both centralize work — they trade differently.

| Aspect | Gateway | Mesh |
|---|---|---|
| Traffic | North-south | East-west |
| Latency | ~1-5 ms p50 | ~1-4 ms/hop |
| Risk | Single door | Fleet to run |
| Code change | None | None |

A gateway concentrates edge logic, so run it redundantly. A mesh buys mTLS and retries with no code change, but you now operate sidecars plus a control plane.

blocks.subTitle: Do you even need a mesh?
blocks.markdown:
The mesh earns its keep at scale, not as a reflex.

- **External clients needing auth/rate-limit/TLS** → API gateway at the edge.
- **Two-plus frontends with different shapes** → BFFs, one per client.
- **Dozens of internal services wanting zero-trust mTLS + uniform resilience** → service mesh.
- **A handful of services or one language** → skip the mesh; a client library or plain LB is simpler. The mesh tax isn't worth it yet.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems
blocks.markdown:
The same proxy ideas show up under different names.

- **Envoy (Lyft)** — the high-performance proxy under most meshes and many gateways; dynamically configured via xDS, so a control plane reshapes routing live.
- **Istio** — the common control plane on Envoy; declarative mTLS and traffic shifting, famous for power at the cost of complexity.
- **Linkerd** — a deliberately simpler mesh with a tiny Rust micro-proxy; do less, but be fast and light.
- **Kong / AWS API Gateway / Netflix Zuul** — classic gateways; Zuul popularized the edge-gateway and BFF patterns ([b05-caching](b05-caching.md)).

blocks.subTitle: Tracing one request
blocks.markdown:
A mobile user opens order history — watch the edge and the mesh cooperate.

```text
1. mobile -> gateway (HTTPS + JWT)
2. gateway: terminate TLS, verify JWT, check rate limit
3. BFF fans out in parallel:
     orders  = GET orders-service/...
     user    = GET users-service/...
     payment = GET payments-service/...
4. each call enters mesh: sidecar opens mTLS
5. Orders returns 503 -> sidecar retries -> success
6. BFF trims + combines -> one JSON back to mobile
```

- One **retry** hid a failure; one **aggregation** turned 3 mobile round trips into 1.

The mistakes that bite in interviews and production:

- **"A mesh replaces the gateway."** Different traffic — edge (N-S) vs internal (E-W). Most large systems need both.
- **Business logic in the gateway.** Keep it *generic*; domain rules belong in the services, or the gateway becomes a hidden monolith.
- **"Control plane down = dead."** No — sidecars keep flowing on last-known config; you only lose the ability to change it.
- **"Retries are free safety."** Mass retries pile load onto a sick service — a **retry storm**. Pair with backoff and caps.
- **"Edge TLS means inside is insecure."** Fine if you re-encrypt internally — exactly what mesh mTLS does.
